idiom_name: Web Crypto (lib DOM / @types/node typings) over the platform primitives
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds types, not cryptography: the primitives come from the runtime - the Web Crypto API (crypto.subtle) in browsers, workers and Node, and node:crypto on the server - while the type definitions come from the lib configuration ("lib": ["DOM", "ES2022"] for WebCrypto in the browser, @types/node for node:crypto). The public mechanism is the algorithm object (AES-GCM, ECDSA with a named curve, PBKDF2) and the secret is a CryptoKey or server-side key material; types help keep parameters explicit (an AesGcmParams instead of an ad-hoc object) but cannot keep a secret - anything bundled for the browser is readable, so hidden "client secrets" remain security by obscurity. On the server, use node:crypto's OpenSSL-backed primitives, never a JavaScript reimplementation of a cipher.
pitfalls: Types are erased at runtime: a CryptoKey-typed variable can be assigned raw bytes from anywhere, and a key bundled for the browser is still public - only server-side secrets stay secret.

A project compiled with the wrong lib set ("lib": ["DOM"] in Node, or @types/node while targeting the web) can silently pick a different crypto implementation; import the runtime's own crypto explicitly and keep the ambient types aligned with the target.
Ambient types can hide a hand-rolled cipher behind a tidy interface (a class Encryptor that XORs); what makes the mechanism reviewable is the public, named algorithm, not the API shape.
